key_insight: Horizontal throughflow leaves temporal convection onset unchanged but raises the absolute-instability threshold, determined by one globally selected off-axis saddle pair.
engineering_relevance: The exact thresholds can guide porous-media thermal design by quantifying how throughflow, resistance and magnetic fields suppress growth at a fixed location.
method: Identify contributing saddles through Fourier-contour deformation and rule out Stokes transitions.
Derive the boundary polynomial and recover frequency to select its physical branch.
Rescale the result across related models and certify convergence of weak- and strong-throughflow expansions.
evidence_signal: Tabulated thresholds check the analytical reduction, while rational certificates establish exact convergence radii for both asymptotic series.
watch_item: The boundary polynomial includes nonphysical branches, so implementations must retain the saddle-selection and frequency-recovery criteria.
paper_title: Global saddle selection and exact absolute-instability boundaries for convection in porous media with throughflow
